messages:
Jamie (Product): Quick sync — Sales is pushing to ship 'Private Connect' POC for a big EU customer next quarter; they're asking we don't block on SOC2. thoughts?
Sara (Security): Not a fan of shipping without controls. Can we scoped-carve a beta with compensating controls? Need legal + infra signoff.
Mike (Engineering): Private Connect involves VPC peering, dedicated pool, and some infra plumbing. Ballpark: 3 dev sprints + 1 for hardening.
Anita (Legal): GDPR/data processing is the trick here. We can do a limited beta but need a clear contract & DPA addendum. Also export controls if data crosses regions.
Leo (Sales): Customer renewal in June. If we delay for SOC2 they walk. They’re okay with a contract-limited beta and NDA.
Jamie (Product): Thinking: RICE it. Impact seems high for revenue, reach small. Effort high. Confidence medium. Want to balance risk vs runway.
Sara (Security): For beta we must have: encryption at rest, TLS, IP allowlist, audit logs, and an off-ramp plan. Also no public marketing as "compliant."
Mike (Engineering): Workaround: restricted beta on a dedicated pool per customer + infra tag to avoid shared KV cache. That reduces immediate scope for SOC2 evidence.
Anita (Legal): NDAs help but don't replace contractual protections. We'll need termination clauses and data deletion commitments. If EU data is involved, process location matters.
Jamie (Product): Proposal: ship Restricted Beta (3 customers max) with dedicated pool, mandatory beta contract, and security checklist. Parallel-run SOC2 control implementation next quarter. GA only after SOC2 or a formal risk decision.
Leo (Sales): That’s acceptable if we can provide a timeline and signed beta agreement. Customer wants 6 weeks.
Mike (Engineering): 6 weeks is tight. With 2 engineers full-time we can do an MVP + infra in ~6w, but no bells. Need budget for reserved GPUs.
Sara (Security): We'll accept compensating controls short-term but require a SOC2 roadmap with milestones. No indefinite betas.
Jamie (Product): Launch criteria (must-haves): perf SLO met, audit logging enabled, legal sign-off on beta, security checklist passed. Must not be marketed as SOC2.
Anita (Legal): I’ll draft the beta agreement & DPA addendum. Will include GDPR/processing terms and a clause for quick termination if controls fail.
Jamie (Product): Quick RICE sketch I’ll share: Reach=2 customers, Impact=8 (revenue retention), Confidence=0.6, Effort=9 engineer-weeks. Putting that into the formula tilts towards taking it as beta.
Mike (Engineering): Note: this will push back the 'batching improvements' work. We should surface to prioritization board if we pivot.
Jamie (Product): Agreed — I'll add it to the next roadmap review with a short memo comparing RICE vs security cost of delay.
Leo (Sales): +1. If we can show compensating controls and timeline, team is fine. :thumbsup:
Sara (Security): +1 but insist on timeline for SOC2 control rollout. I'll prepare the minimal checklist we need.
Deploy-bot: Deployment window reserved for dev sandbox on 2024-05-15 03:00 UTC.
Mike (Engineering): I’ll create ticket INF-2345 and assign tasks.
Jamie (Product): Thanks all — action items: @Anita draft beta contract, @Sara prepare checklist, @Mike scope infra + cost, @Leo confirm customer OK with limited beta. I’ll follow up with a short RICE doc tomorrow.
Anita (Legal): Will send first draft by EOD tomorrow.
Sara (Security): I’ll post the checklist and SOC2 milestone plan this week.
Jamie (Product): Great. If anyone has objections to the restricted-beta approach, speak now or file in the roadmap thread. Otherwise I’ll move forward.
Leo (Sales): No objections from me.
Mike (Engineering): 👍
Jamie (Product): Closing thread — thanks everyone.
